headline: Price gains and a hydrovac deal lift sales and margins
summary_short: Toro's fiscal Q2 2026 (three months ended May 1, 2026) net sales rose 8.1% y/y to $1,424.7M, gross margin expanded 80bps to 33.9%, and net earnings grew 6.3% y/y to $145.4M ($1.50 diluted GAAP EPS, $1.60 adjusted); the sequential jump from Q1 reflects normal spring-season seasonality, not a step-change.
summary_long: Growth was driven by net price realization, the Tornado Infrastructure Equipment acquisition ($29.7M of Q2 sales, Professional segment), and higher shipments in both segments; Professional sales rose 9.1% y/y with EBIT margin up to 20.3% from 19.9%, while Residential sales rose 4.4% y/y with EBIT margin nearly doubling to 9.8% from 5.4% on price, productivity gains, and non-recurring prior-year inventory adjustments. Gross margin expanded 80bps y/y on pricing and productivity, partly offset by higher material/freight costs. AMP delivered $106.8M of cumulative savings toward a raised $125M fiscal-2027 run-rate target. First-half free cash flow was $265.5M (vs $84.7M a year ago); the company repurchased $192.1M of stock and paid a $0.39/share dividend. No FY2026 guidance figures appear in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Sales and margin gains were driven by net price realization, productivity improvements under the AMP initiative, and the Tornado Infrastructure Equipment acquisition, partially offset by higher material, manufacturing, and freight costs.
Growth was primarily driven by net price realization, the Tornado acquisition, and higher shipments of both Professional and Residential segment products.
The 80bps y/y increase was primarily due to net price realization and productivity improvements, partially offset by higher material, manufacturing, and freight costs and product mix.
Tracks the gross-margin and segment-EBIT gains described above; the release attributes the quarter's earnings growth to price realization and productivity gains across both segments.
Per-share (adjusted) growth was primarily due to higher Professional and Residential segment earnings, partially offset by higher corporate expenses and productivity initiative charges.

Tracks net-earnings growth; acquisition-related costs ($3.5M) and productivity-initiative charges ($7.3M) reduced GAAP operating earnings relative to the $205.8M adjusted figure this quarter, per the company's own reconciliation.

Not explained separately in the release; EBIT is a Yahoo-timeseries-derived measure that is not a line item disclosed in the 10-Q, so no company-stated cause exists for this specific figure beyond the GAAP operating-earnings drivers above.

Not explained separately in the release; EBITDA is a Yahoo-timeseries-derived measure not disclosed as a line item in the 10-Q, so its movement tracks the GAAP operating-earnings and depreciation/amortization trends rather than a stated cause.
